CG Weather Today: छत्तीसगढ़ में मानसून सक्रिय बना हुआ है। प्रदेश के कई हिस्सों में हल्की से मध्यम बारिश का दौर जारी है। मौसम विभाग के रायपुर केंद्र ने 22 अगस्त 2026 को सुबह 4 बजे जारी चेतावनी में बस्तर जिले के लिए ऑरेंज अलर्ट जारी किया है। यहां अलग-अलग स्थानों पर मध्यम बारिश के साथ गरज-चमक और बिजली गिरने की संभावना जताई गई है।
मौसम विभाग की चेतावनी के अनुसार बस्तर में यह अलर्ट 22 अगस्त को सुबह 4 बजे से सुबह 7 बजे तक प्रभावी है। वहीं छह जिलों के लिए येलो अलर्ट जारी किया गया है। इनमें गौरेला-पेंड्रा-मरवाही, मुंगेली, कबीरधाम, बीजापुर, दंतेवाड़ा और सुकमा शामिल हैं। इन जिलों में अलग-अलग स्थानों पर हल्की बारिश के साथ गरज-चमक होने की संभावना है।
अगले सात दिन सक्रिय रहेगा मानसून
मौसम विभाग के 21 अगस्त को जारी पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार छत्तीसगढ़ में अगले सात दिनों तक बारिश का दौर जारी रहने की संभावना है। 22 से 27 अगस्त तक प्रदेश के अधिकांश स्थानों पर हल्की से मध्यम बारिश हो सकती है। इस दौरान एक-दो स्थानों पर भारी बारिश के साथ गरज-चमक और वज्रपात की भी संभावना जताई गई है।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार अगले पांच दिनों में प्रदेश के अधिकतम तापमान में कोई विशेष बदलाव होने की संभावना नहीं है।
पिछले 24 घंटे में कई इलाकों में हुई बारिश
पिछले 24 घंटों में प्रदेश के अनेक स्थानों पर हल्की से मध्यम बारिश दर्ज की गई। मौसम विभाग के आंकड़ों के अनुसार दुर्ग में 16.6 मिलीमीटर, राजनांदगांव में 14 मिलीमीटर, माना विमानतल में 4.1 मिलीमीटर और लालपुर रायपुर में 2.8 मिलीमीटर बारिश दर्ज की गई। पेण्ड्रारोड में 2.6 मिलीमीटर तथा जगदलपुर में 0.8 मिलीमीटर बारिश हुई।
मौसम विभाग ने बताया कि प्रदेश में मौसमी उप-विभागीय बारिश सामान्य रही है और इसमें सामान्य से 7 प्रतिशत का अंतर दर्ज किया गया है।
रायपुर में भी बारिश के आसार
राजधानी रायपुर में भी बादल छाए रहने के साथ बारिश होने की संभावना बनी हुई है। मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक रायपुर शहर में एक-दो बार बारिश या गरज-चमक के साथ बौछारें पड़ सकती हैं। अधिकतम तापमान करीब 28 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान करीब 24 डिग्री रहने का अनुमान है।
बिजली गिरने के दौरान बरतें सावधानी
मौसम विभाग ने गरज-चमक और वज्रपात के दौरान लोगों को सुरक्षित स्थानों पर रहने की सलाह दी है। गड़गड़ाहट सुनाई देने पर घर के अंदर या सुरक्षित पक्के आश्रय में जाने को कहा गया है।
विभाग ने लोगों को पेड़ों के नीचे आश्रय लेने से बचने, बिजली की लाइनों से दूर रहने और बिजली एवं इलेक्ट्रॉनिक उपकरणों का इस्तेमाल नहीं करने की सलाह दी है।
किसानों को खुले में रखे कृषि उत्पादों को बारिश से बचाने के लिए सुरक्षित स्थान पर रखने की सलाह दी गई है। वहीं बागवानों और सब्जी उत्पादकों को ओलावृष्टि की स्थिति में उपलब्धता के आधार पर एंटी हेल नेट का इस्तेमाल करने की सलाह दी गई है।

Bust Fake News With Bangalore Mirror: Say cheese: Heat is on, but no crisis situation so far
.
CLAIM: Extreme heat is creating a “Great Parmesan Crisis” threatening both Parmigiano Reggiano cheese and Italy’s “cheese banks”, where hundreds of thousands of wheels are stored as loan collateral.
FACT: Misleading, the beloved cheese is safely stored in cool conditions and ageing nicely while the rest of Italy swelters. MGT, which stores 500,000 cheese wheels valued at €300 million ($350 million) across two facilities, confirmed that all is well.
As Italy swelters under a period of extreme heat, social media accounts have circulated exaggerated and false claims that soaring temperatures are threatening Parmigiano Reggiano cheese and the banks that store the wheels as collateral for loans.
Parmigiano Reggiano is produced under strict regulations in defined areas of northern Italy’s Emilia-Romagna region. The hard cheese is made from milk produced by cattle fed locally grown forage. Each wheel must be aged for at least 12 months, although many are matured for 24, 36 or even 40 months.
Because producers often have to wait years before their cheese can be sold, a handful of banks accept the wheels as collateral for loans during the ageing process. The largest of these is Credito Emiliano S.p.A.’s Magazzini Generali delle Tagliate (MGT), which has operated since 1953.
Social media posts claimed that the extreme heat sweeping Italy had created a “Great Parmesan Crisis”, putting both the cheese and the country’s so-called “cheese banks” at risk. The reality, however, is considerably less dramatic.
MGT stores around 500,000 cheese wheels, worth about €300 million ($350 million), across two facilities. The company confirmed that the extreme temperatures, which have regularly approached 40 degrees Celsius this summer, have not endangered either the cheese or its operations.
Giancarlo Ravanetti, MGT’s general manager, said energy consumption had increased by about 30% as the warehouses worked harder to maintain the cool conditions required for ageing the cheese.
Despite the higher energy demand, the facilities have continued operating normally, with the wheels kept under optimal storage conditions. Ravanetti said he did not expect longer-term consequences, even if extreme heat becomes more frequent in the future.
MGT has improved warehouse efficiency by upgrading refrigeration, insulation and installing 1.5MW of solar power.
However, extreme heat can affect dairy cattle and reduce milk yields by around 10%. The Parmigiano Reggiano consortium said production is not currently at risk.
Farmers use preserved forage, fans, water-spraying systems and environmental monitoring to protect cattle. About 70% of the milk comes from farms equipped with cooling measures, while the rest is sourced from cooler hill and mountain areas.
So, while Italy bakes, its prized Parmesan remains safely stored and ageing. — AP

title: Surrey veterinary hospital warns of heat and dehydration risks for pets - The Malone Telegram

full_text:
Boundary Bay Veterinary Specialty Hospital reports severe, often preventable heat-related and dehydration cases across Metro Vancouver
SURREY, British Columbia - August 21, 2026 - Boundary Bay Veterinary Specialty Hospital (BBVSH) is cautioning pet owners across Metro Vancouver that continuing seasonal heat can push dogs and cats into life-threatening emergencies within minutes, from heatstroke in parked vehicles to serious dehydration. The hospital's Emergency and Critical Care Service reports an increase in both conditions, many of which are preventable with early recognition and timely care.
The hospital reminds the community that the interior of a parked vehicle heats rapidly because cars trap heat and limit air circulation, and cracking a window provides little protection. Dogs and cats cannot cool themselves as efficiently as humans do, relying instead on panting and other limited mechanisms that can quickly become overwhelmed. BBVSH’s board-certified veterinary specialists emphasize that heatstroke is a multisystem emergency that can affect the kidneys, gastrointestinal tract, clotting system, nervous system, and cardiovascular system, and that internal injury can persist for hours after a pet appears to recover.
Dehydration is closely linked to heat but is often more serious than a missed bowl of water. The hospital explains that fluid loss affects circulation, kidney function, and temperature regulation, and may signal an underlying condition such as gastrointestinal disease, kidney disease, diabetes, or infection. Warning signs of both conditions can include lethargy, weakness, dry or tacky gums, sunken eyes, and excessive panting.
The hospital notes that cats warrant particular attention because their naturally lower thirst drive can make fluid deficits harder to detect. Brachycephalic breeds, senior and very young animals, overweight pets, and those with heart or respiratory conditions face elevated risk.
"A pet can look comfortable one moment and become critically ill the next, and the damage does not always stop once they cool down," said Emily Puntney-Vogt, Emergency Veterinarian at Boundary Bay Veterinary Specialty Hospital. "If your pet cannot come inside with you, the safest choice is to leave them at home, and when signs of illness appear, seeking care early can make a real difference."
The hospital advises owners to provide constant access to fresh water, offer shade, and avoid strenuous activity during the hottest parts of the day. Anyone who sees a distressed pet in a hot vehicle in British Columbia should note the vehicle details and contact local police, RCMP, animal control, or the BC SPCA Animal Helpline, as only designated enforcement personnel have legal authority to remove an animal.
Pet owners can read the hospital's full summer safety guidance and blogs at https://bbvsh.com/
About Boundary Bay Veterinary Specialty Hospital
Boundary Bay Veterinary Specialty Hospital is an independent, family-owned specialty, emergency and critical care hospital in Surrey, BC. Open 24/7/365 and equipped to handle even the most critical emergencies and trauma, they support pets across Metro Vancouver and throughout BC from their convenient location just off Hwy 1.
On-site services include animal rehabilitation, veterinary behaviour medicine, veterinary cardiology, veterinary dentistry, veterinary diagnostic imaging, veterinary internal medicine, veterinary oncology, veterinary neurology and veterinary surgery.
Boundary Bay Veterinary Specialty Hospital is located at 10436 173 St, Surrey, BC V4N 5H3.

The DANA breaks in with hail in Reus amid a heat alert of 35 degrees
The Camp de Tarragona and Reus face a DANA with storms and hail. The instability coincides with the alert for extreme heat and a risk of rain that will exceed 90% on the weekend.
Reus and the Camp de Tarragona area will enter an episode of storms, heavy rain, and hail starting this Thursday due to the arrival of a DANA, with instability expected until the weekend. Meteocat places the start of precipitation in Les Terres de l'Ebre and anticipates it will then advance towards the Tarragona regions.
The change comes amidst a heat alert. Protecció Civil maintains the pre-alert of the Inuncat Plan due to the possibility of downpours exceeding 20 liters per square meter in 30 minutes and, at the same time, has activated the alert phase of the Procicat for intense heat and nighttime heat.
Les Terres de l'Ebre will receive the first rains before the front advances towards Reus
The regions included in this episode are Baix Camp, Tarragonès, Priorat, Conca de Barberà, Alt Camp, Baix Penedès, and Les Terres de l'Ebre.
In Reus, a maximum of 35 degrees is expected this Thursday. The probability of precipitation will be 40% between 12 PM and 6 PM, a period that will coincide with the highest heat of the day and increased instability.
The risk of rain will grow with the hours. For Friday afternoon, the forecast rises to 75%, on Saturday morning it reaches 90%, and between Sunday and Monday it will range between 60% and 80%.
Protecció Civil maintains the pre-alert for rain while the heat warning continues
Protecció Civil has placed the Inuncat Plan on pre-alert due to the possibility of intense downpours in several parts of Camp de Tarragona and Les Terres de l'Ebre. The threshold that activates monitoring is more than 20 liters per square meter in half an hour.
Furthermore, the agency maintains the warning for intense daytime heat for this Wednesday with a maximum danger level of three out of six. Added to this situation is the alert phase of the Procicat for intense heat and nighttime heat, a scenario that links to the increase in fires in Camp de Tarragona during this summer.
During the weekend, maximum temperatures will remain close to 30 degrees.
Minimum temperatures will also continue at high values, typical of the month of August.
